To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the US and Europe have similar policy goals for pharmaceutical cost containment, and that they use similar evidence-based approaches.

there is a convergence in the objectives of pharmaceutical policy between the US and EU countries, but that the evidence-based approaches used to achieve these objectives are shaped by politics and are therefore not converging.

(i) the US and Europe appear to be moving towards convergence in their objectives of pharmaceutical policy; (ii) policymakers are increasingly resorting to the same evidence-based approaches to address these objectives; and (iii) the development and implementation processes of these approaches are a function of politics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of evidence-based approaches to improve the efficiency and equity of pharmaceutical reimbursement.
understanding how and why the evidence is used to make decisions about pharmaceutical policy in the US and in Europe.
the politics of evidence-based policy making, and how this affects the development and implementation process for new drug appraisement for reimbursement.

there is no evidence that the US and Europe have converged in terms of the development and implementation approaches for evidence-based policy making, although there is some evidence for convergence in terms of policy objectives.
the evidence-based approach is not the same across all countries and settings within countries.
there is no convergence in the development and application of evidence-based policy tools to achieve the policy objectives of cost containment, access and clinical practice variation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are moving towards convergence of policy objectives but not necessarily convergence of approaches.
we have found that there is a lot of evidence-based medicine, but not a lot of evidence-informed policy making.
the evidence-based approaches to prescription drug policy in the US and the EU are not only converging but also diverging, depending on the specific issue.

the US and Europe may be moving closer to each other in terms of the evidence they rely upon to make decisions about the use of pharmaceuticals.
, although there is movement towards convergence, there are also instances of divergence in how evidence-based approaches are developed and implemented.
the US and European policymakers are converging on the use of evidence-based approaches, but the evidence they use, how they use it, and what they do with it, will differ.
